newsitem.title: UK: British govt reaffirms commitment to minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: British govt reaffirms commitment to minimum wage.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government has begun preparatory work on the introduction of a national minimium wage, trade and industry junior minister Ian McCartney said.

"It will be set at a sensible level, taking account of the economic circumstances of the time, and will narrow the poverty gap by enabling individual workers to be better off in work than they would be if unemployed and living on state benefits," he said in his first speech as Minister for Social Partnership.

He told a trade union conference in Bournemouth that the government was already working on setting up an independent Low Pay Commission, including representatives of businesses and employees, which will make recommendations to the government on the level at which the minimum wage should be set. "This Government will legislate for a minimum wage as quickly as possible so that we can remove the worst excesses of low pay and exploitation of workers," McCartney said.
